item.title: How do you clean a fabric sofa?
item.description: Read the cleaning code, vacuum first, blot instead of scrub, use little liquid, and dry at room temperature. Stop before you leave a ring.

item.title: State of the Upholstery Trade
item.description: Open survey data from working upholsterers worldwide: shop rates, bench hours by piece, fabric markup, lead times and which work actually pays.

item.title: Contents — Learn to Upholster
item.description: The full contents of The Working Upholsterer's Bible — foundations, techniques, complete projects, the working workshop, and reference. Free to read.

item.title: A Brief, Opinionated History of Upholstery
item.description: A brief, opinionated history of upholstery — from mediaeval cushions and Tudor state beds to Pratt’s coil spring, the staple gun, and today’s craft revival.

item.title: Upholstery Fabric Yardage Calculator: Metric & Imperial
item.description: How much fabric to reupholster a chair or sofa? A free calculator in metres and yards, a rule-of-thumb chart, and how to allow for pattern repeats.

item.title: Pricing & Quoting for an Upholstery Workshop
item.description: How to price upholstery work and build a quote that survives: setting an hourly rate from an income target, the materials / labour / contingency breakdown.

item.title: Customers & the Upholstery Workshop Year
item.description: The business side of upholstery: the first customer conversation, managing expectations, quoting with confidence, and the seasonal rhythm of the year.

item.title: A–Z glossary of upholstery terms
item.description: An A-Z of around 150 upholstery terms, from antimacassar to zigzag spring, in plain English and cross-referenced to the relevant chapters.

item.title: UK Upholstery Standards, Regulations & Bibliography
item.description: The administrative side of UK upholstery: the Furniture and Furnishings (Fire) (Safety) Regulations, an FR-materials checklist, the trade bodies worth.

item.title: Reupholstery Cost & Time Estimator
item.description: A free reupholstery cost calculator: pick your piece, build type and fabric, and get a ballpark price and bench-hours estimate — based on a working West.

item.title: About
item.description: Learn to Upholster is a free upholstery reference and companion to the book The Working Upholsterer's Bible, by master upholsterer Shaun Greenwood.

item.title: Find an Upholsterer Near You: UK, US & Worldwide
item.description: How to find a good upholsterer near you: search the vetted AMUSF member directory in the UK, find local upholsterers on the map anywhere, and the questions.

item.title: Buy the Book: Wiro-Bound Workshop Edition
item.description: The wiro-bound A4 workshop edition of The Working Upholsterer's Bible: 35 chapters, 72 figures, lies flat on the bench. Printed to order in the UK.

item.title: Upholstery Projects — Real Jobs, Documented
item.description: Real upholstery jobs documented stage by stage from a working AMUSF workshop: furniture, campervans, motorbike seats, plant machinery and soft furnishings.

item.title: Business Hub — free resources for working upholsterers
item.description: Free business resources for working upholsterers: pricing, quoting, finding customers, running a workshop and making a living from the craft.

item.title: Take part in the survey
item.description: Add your workshop to the State of the Upholstery Trade survey. Anonymous, thirteen questions, about three minutes.

item.title: Free Printable Upholstery Workshop Forms
item.description: Four free printable forms for an upholstery workshop: customer enquiry, condition report, job sheet, and delivery note. No download, no account.

item.title: Upholstery supplier directory
item.description: Verified upholstery suppliers across the UK, US, Canada, Australia and New Zealand: traditional materials, foam, fabric and tools. Nobody pays to be listed.

item.title: United States Upholstery Fire Regulations
item.description: Federal standard since 2021, and it names reupholstery — but not when the piece keeps the same owner.

item.title: Upholstery fire regulations by country
item.description: Upholstery fire regulations by country: United Kingdom, United States, Canada, Australia & New Zealand. Domestic and commercial requirements, sourced and date

item.title: Australia & New Zealand Upholstery Fire Regulations
item.description: The AS/NZS upholstery flammability standards are voluntary. There is no mandatory domestic requirement in either country.

item.title: Canada upholstery fire regulations
item.description: No flammability standard for upholstered furniture. All three provincial schemes were repealed between 2019 and 2021.

item.title: Ireland upholstery fire regulations
item.description: Its own 1995 Order and Irish Standard, close to the British regime but a separate legal instrument.

item.title: Industrial sewing for upholsterers
item.description: Industrial sewing for upholsterers: thread, needles, machines and troubleshooting, explained from an upholstery bench rather than a sail loft.

item.title: Sewing machine needles for upholstery
item.description: Upholstery needle sizes by thread size, needle systems, round and leather points, and why a blunt needle causes skipped stitches.

item.title: Upholstery Thread Guide: Sizes, Nylon vs Polyester
item.description: Which upholstery thread for which job: bonded nylon or polyester, Tex sizes, commercial and government numbering, and needle pairing.

item.title: Thread & Needle Selector for Upholstery
item.description: Three questions returning the thread, size, needle, point and stitch length for an upholstery job, with the reasoning for each.

item.title: Industrial Sewing Machines for Upholstery
item.description: Industrial sewing machines for upholstery: drop, needle, walking foot and compound feed explained, plus flat, cylinder, post and long arm beds.

item.title: Sewing Machine Troubleshooting for Upholstery
item.description: Upholstery sewing machine troubleshooting: skipped stitches, thread breaking, puckering, tension and feed problems, in the order worth checking.

item.title: Sewing Machine Setup & Parts for Upholstery
item.description: Servo against clutch motors, speed reducers, presser feet for upholstery, and the order to set tension in.

item.title: Blog
item.description: Notes from the workshop bench: materials, problems, and the questions customers actually ask.

item.title: Why does leather peel?
item.description: Real leather does not peel. What peels is bonded leather or a polyurethane coating — how to tell which you have, why it fails, and what can actually be repaired.

item.title: Why does velvet go patchy?
item.description: Velvet does not go patchy — it shades. Why pile fabric changes colour as it is pressed, which velvets recover and which mark permanently, and what pile direction does to your fabric quantity.

item.title: Why has my sofa gone saggy in the middle?
item.description: Something under the cushions has failed, and it is usually not the cushions. How to tell whether it is the foam, the webbing, the springs or the frame — and which of those is worth fixing.

item.title: Is it cheaper to reupholster or buy new?
item.description: Usually not, if you compare it to the cheapest new sofa in the sale — but that is the wrong comparison. What actually decides it is the frame, and how to check yours in two minutes.

item.title: What's the best upholstery fabric if you have a dog?
item.description: The construction matters more than the fibre. Why loops are the thing to avoid, which fabrics genuinely survive claws and hair, and the colour trick nobody mentions.

item.title: How to look after a leather sofa
item.description: Which finish you have decides everything, and there is a two-minute test that tells you. The routine that keeps leather alive for decades, and the everyday products that quietly destroy it.

item.title: Why do two upholsterers quote such different prices?
item.description: Usually because they are not quoting for the same work. The recover-versus-reupholster distinction, what gets replaced underneath, and the five questions that make quotes actually comparable.

item.title: Why is my sofa fabric bobbling?
item.description: Pilling is loose fibre working to the surface, and it is usually not a fault. Why blends pill worst, why it normally stops on its own, and the separate test standard nobody tells you to ask about.
